Random-effect marginal covariance update plan

Source: R/random-effects-marginal-update.R
random_effects_marginal_update_plan.Rd

Resolves a selected public random-effect quantity to the exact scalar dependence of its marginal covariance contribution. The result is compiled exclusively from the fitted parameter map and formula random-effect metadata; posterior draws are neither inspected nor used to infer an update form. An unsupported plan can include a conditional entry containing required_active and plan. The nested plan applies only to posterior rows where every named inclusion indicator equals one. It does not declare an unconditional update for the selected public quantity.

random_effects_marginal_update_plan(fit, selection)

Arguments

fit

a fitted object carrying a BayesTools parameter map and formula design metadata.

selection

a one-quantity selection returned by parameter_catalog_resolve().

Value

A list of class BayesTools_random_effects_marginal_update_plan. Field family is one of "affine", "factor", "markov", or "unsupported". An affine plan additionally records the scalar covariance coefficient transform and the affected random-effect blocks. For a plan in a source coordinate (coefficient_input = "source"), the blocks include every block whose SD binding uses that source, also through another variance allocation.

Fields shared by the supported families are update (the kind of update, below), blocks, structure and component_index (the covariance structure and the column of a per-column quantity), coefficient_input, source_parameter, source_transform and source_transform_spec (the fitted coordinate and its transform to the public quantity), quantity_id, canonical_name, formula_parameter and dependencies. Affine plans add coefficient_transform and, for the Dirichlet-weight updates of an allocation, allocation (weight_name, index, n_targets, and the allocation scale when the plan comes from the conditional route). invariant_covariance holds the covariance that does not depend on the selected coordinate when it is structurally available, and NULL otherwise. Factor plans of allocation-derived SDs add coefficient_scale_transform. An unsupported plan carries reason and message instead.

update is "scale" when the contribution of the affected blocks is scaled by one coefficient, "column_scale" when the SDs of some columns of a block change (component_index, the first column of the selected SD; the other column SDs of a direct per-column SD are held fixed, a direct SD shared by several columns lists them in driven_columns, and so do the driven columns of an allocation-derived SD), "allocation" when a Dirichlet weight of a variance allocation changes, and "correlation" for a correlation coordinate. A direct per-column SD with unequal column SDs reports "column_scale".

The plan of an allocation-derived component SD or variance, and of an aggregate allocation SD or variance (sd_common, var_common, sd_total, var_total) that is a quantity-scale plan, has the field held_fixed = "allocation_weights": whatever the covariance structure, setting the selected SD to v holds the allocation weights and every non-allocation coordinate (correlations included) fixed and moves the allocation scale tau of the SD SD_k = tau * m_k(w) to v / m_k(w), where m_k(w) is the product of the square roots of the weights on the path from tau to the SD (sqrt(w_j) for a total-variance allocation, sqrt(K_j w_j) for a mean-variance one, over the nested allocations). This is the conditional of the variance prior declared on (tau, w), which are independent a priori. For an SD value v the prior of the moved coordinate is the tau prior evaluated at v / m_k(w) with the Jacobian 1 / m_k(w); for a variance value u the SD is sqrt(u) and the Jacobian is 1 / m_k(w)^2 on the variance parameterization of the scale (tau^2, equivalently 1 / (2 m_k(w) sqrt(u)) from tau). The scale reaches every block whose SD binding uses it, also through nested allocations (a split root with one <block>_components allocation per block) or a shared random_sd_source(): blocks lists all of them, the selected block first. Every column SD that derives from tau is multiplied by the same factor c = v / SD_k, so a reached block whose columns are all driven by tau has its covariance contribution multiplied by c^2 on every covariance structure: the plan is then the affine update = "scale" plan of the summed contribution of blocks. If tau drives only some columns of the selected block, which is the only block it reaches, the plan is the factor "column_scale" plan with driven_columns and the grid factor column_factor for them, when the selected column is among the driven ones (otherwise the plan is unsupported with the reason "selected_column_not_driven"); a scale that reaches several blocks and only part of their columns, or an aggregate whose scale drives only part of a block, has no exact scalar update and is unsupported with the reason "partial_scale_reach". An aggregate of a nested allocation moves the root scale of its allocation chain as well, so its blocks are those of every sibling allocation of the root, not only its own. Plans of direct per-column SDs have no held_fixed field.

Details

family = "affine" means that, conditional on every non-selected posterior coordinate, the row covariance has the exact form A + h(value) * B, where value is the coordinate declared by coefficient_input ("source" or "quantity") and h is recorded in coefficient_transform. family = "factor" identifies an exact candidate-dependent covariance factor, while family = "markov" identifies a compiled structured Markov state. Allocation-derived component SDs are affine on every covariance structure when the allocation scale drives all columns of every block it reaches (A + h(v) B with h the square of the SD or the identity of the variance, B the summed covariance of blocks per unit of h); they are factor column_scale updates only when it drives part of the columns of the one block it reaches. All of them hold the allocation weights fixed and scale every driven column SD by the same factor (held_fixed, above), so the column_scale plan of an allocation-derived SD differs from that of a direct SD, which replaces the scale of its own columns only (one column, or every column in driven_columns for an SD shared by several columns). Their coefficient_scale_transform converts a selected variance to its square root and leaves a selected SD unchanged. These quantity-scale plans require the public SD to be on the fitted coefficient scale; after formula scaling that changes it, the plan is unsupported. Unsupported plans carry a structural reason. The accessor never estimates affineness from evaluated covariance matrices.

The invariant covariance of a block with several coefficient columns is a dense rows x rows matrix of the fitted data. Its estimated peak memory is checked against the BayesTools.random_effects_memory_limit_bytes option (see BayesTools) before it is formed; above the ceiling the accessor stops with an error of class BayesTools_random_effects_memory_limit (also BayesTools_random_effects_error).

The conditional entry of an unsupported plan is compiled only for a variance allocation with exactly two single-column block targets, a scalar total-variance source and inclusion gates on the blocks; an allocation with more than two targets has no conditional plan and stays unsupported.
